request: Analyze GSE75919 for PMID 27304508 (Osteocalcin Signaling in Myofibers Is Necessary and Sufficient for Optimum Adaptation to Exercise.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.primary_estimand: Genotype effect (Gprc6a_Mck-/- vs Gprc6a fl/fl) on muscle gene expression after a single bout of treadmill exercise; all sequenced mice were exercised
planned_contrasts: Gprc6a_Mck-/- vs Gprc6a fl/fl, both after exercise (S2.5.p1, S4.3.p1; paper reports no DEG count, names Il6 as most decreased (80%) and a modest decrease of Il6ra, Figure 6A/S6A)

exercise: after exercise only (no sedentary arm sequenced)

final.exercise_protocol: single bout, 40 min treadmill at 30 cm/s (S2.1.p1)

paper_threshold.source_locator: S4.3.p1 (RNA-seq details deferred to supplemental information, not available)

final.paper_method: not stated in main text (supplemental information)
final.paper_results: Il6 most decreased (~80%) in Gprc6a_Mck-/- muscle after exercise; Il6ra modestly decreased; other myokines unaffected

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S2.5.p1: 'we performed a transcriptomic analysis in muscles of control and Gprc6a_Mck-/- mice after exercise'. S4.3.p1: 'The genome-wide differential expression of Gprc6a_Mck-/- vs. Gprc6af/f in muscle was measured by RNASeq'. The RNA-seq is a genotype comparison within exercised mice; the exercise-vs-rest effect was studied only by qPCR/ELISA, not sequenced.

checks: GEO source_name: gastrocnemius muscles of 3 month old mice after exercise
genotype Grpc6afl/fl (5) vs Grpc6afl/fl;Mck-Cre (4) matches the paper's Gprc6a_Mck-/- vs Gprc6af/f
contact lab Karsenty (Columbia), the paper's lab
matrix column names equal GEO description field for all 9 GSMs

ownership.reasoning: Series, tissue, genotypes and lab match the paper's RNA-seq (S2.5.p1, S4.3.p1); the paper does not cite the accession in the main text but no other series is plausible.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns (e.g. a1.wt.Gprc6a.fl/fl.GP2) equal the GEO 'description' field exactly; genotype from characteristics. No exercise column exists: every sample is post-exercise.

matrix.reasoning: All-integer values; data_processing: 'Reads in each gene were counted with HTSeq-0.6.1', 'Xlsx file with raw counts for each gene'. Converted xlsx to CSV without changing values (prep_counts.py).

design.stop_reason: No exercise contrast: all 9 sequenced mice (5 Gprc6a fl/fl, 4 Gprc6a_Mck-/-) were sampled after exercise and no sedentary/rest arm was sequenced, so the effect of exercise on gene expression is not identifiable. The only available contrast is genotype within exercised mice (the paper's RNA-seq estimand), which is not an exercise effect.

candidates.reason_rejected: Estimates a genotype effect under exercise, not how exercise affects gene expression; without a rested group neither the exercise effect nor a genotype x exercise interaction can be estimated.

design.reasoning: GEO source_name is constant ('after exercise') for every sample; paper S2.5.p1 confirms the transcriptome was taken only after exercise. The request asks for the exercise effect; the data hold one factor (genotype) only.

discrepancies.paper: Exercise effect on muscle Il6 assessed by qPCR/ELISA in rested vs exercised mice (Figure 6B-G)
